biggest_catch: The $150 is the maximum and product-specific — smaller upgrades pay less (e.g., $25 for a qualifying refrigerator). You're also buying and installing efficiency upgrades first; the rebate comes after review, not at checkout.
catches: Amounts are per-measure: up to $150 for smart thermostats, up to $800 for heat-pump water heaters, $50 for qualifying washers/dryers, $25 for qualifying refrigerators — you must install a qualifying measure.
Some measures may require pre-approval or a qualifying contractor/installation.
Rebates are paid after submission and review — you pay for the upgrade upfront.
The program covers multiple measures; pick the ones that fit your home — this route scopes to the appliance/thermostat measures on the official page.

eligibility: Georgia Power residential customer. Install a qualifying energy-efficient measure listed on the Home Energy Improvement Program page and submit the rebate claim.

steps: Confirm you're a Georgia Power residential customer.
Pick a qualifying measure from the Home Energy Improvement Program list (e.g., smart thermostat up to $150, qualifying refrigerator $25).
Check whether your measure needs pre-approval before purchase.
Buy and install the qualifying product; keep your receipt.
Submit the rebate claim on the Georgia Power page with your receipt and account info.
timing: Rebate paid after your claim is reviewed and approved.
